update.title: Built a shared history database for system activity
update.summary: Built a PostgreSQL history store for tool operations and artifacts, with a normalized SQLAlchemy schema, repository API, and provenance queries.

preview.description: The first recorded Constellation History Database output and its linked artifacts

blocks.body:
## Give tool activity a shared data model

I built a PostgreSQL history store so Constellation tools can record operations and the files they consume or produce without inventing a separate log format for every integration. The schema gives operations, artifacts, and tags independent records, while relation tables preserve inputs, outputs, categories, and parent-operation chains.

## Preserve lineage through the operation lifecycle

The repository API lets callers start an operation, register inputs as they become known, attach outputs, and finish with success or failure. A convenience path covers work that has already completed. Artifact registration is idempotent by resolved path, allowing later queries to follow an artifact back to the operation that consumed or produced it.

blocks.code:
erDiagram
  OPERATION ||--o{ OPERATION_INPUT : consumes
  ARTIFACT ||--o{ OPERATION_INPUT : is_input
  OPERATION ||--o{ OPERATION_OUTPUT : produces
  ARTIFACT ||--o{ OPERATION_OUTPUT : is_output
  OPERATION }o--o{ TAG : categorized_by
  OPERATION o|--o{ OPERATION : parent_of

  OPERATION {
    uuid id
    string operation_type
    string tool_name
    string status
    timestamp started_at
    timestamp completed_at
    jsonb config
  }
  ARTIFACT {
    uuid id
    text file_path
    string file_type
    string checksum
    jsonb metadata
  }
blocks.description: The schema models operations and artifacts independently, then uses explicit relations for inputs, outputs, tags, and operation chains.

blocks.body:
## Keep the storage boundary inspectable

SQLAlchemy provides the model and repository API, while Alembic manages schema changes. Queries cover recent activity, time ranges, tools, operation types, tags, artifact history, and parent chains. Local peer authentication, direct SQL access, and documented dump and restore procedures keep the history usable outside the Python interface.
